name: Peggy Flanagan

issue_poll.name: KSTP/SurveyUSA Minnesota poll, Aug 13-17, 2026 (single most important issue, 661 likely voters)
issue_poll.note: Latest Minnesota poll found with a full issue ranking. Order: Inflation/cost of living 35%, Fraud 15%, Health care 11%, Immigration 8%, Gas prices 6%, War in Iran 5%, Education 5%, Jobs 4%, Abortion 3%, Crime 2%, Gun control 2%; 'Other' and 'Not sure' dropped. Crime and Gun control tied at 2%; Crime kept at rank 10 by its order in the source table. Earlier Emerson poll (Feb 6-8, 2026) had 'threats to democracy' first at 28%, but SurveyUSA did not offer that option.

issues.detail: Universal child care; ban Wall Street firms from buying homes; end federal tax on Social Security benefits; farm equipment right to repair.
Increase oversight and penalties for fraud; restore independent federal inspectors general.
Enact Medicare for All; restore Medicaid cuts in the 2025 reconciliation law; ban insurer prior authorization.
Dismantle and replace ICE; claw back the $75 billion given to ICE; path to citizenship for long-settled immigrants.
100% carbon-free electricity by 2040; support biofuels and sustainable aviation fuel.
Vote against more funding for the Iran war; oppose additional offensive weapons or military aid to Israel under Netanyahu.
Fund special education (IDEA) at the promised 40% federal share.
Raise federal minimum wage to at least $17/hour indexed to inflation; national paid family and medical leave.
Pass the Women's Health Protection Act; require Medicaid and ACA exchange plans to cover IVF.
Ban assault weapons and high-capacity magazines.

plan_caveats: Issue poll is from mid-August 2026; no Minnesota issue-ranking poll closer to Election Day was found.
Rank 10: Crime and Gun control tied at 2%; Crime chosen by source-table order, and rated on her gun-ban pledge (her other crime items - re-entry programs, police training funds - are not checkable).
Gas prices rated on her energy plan (2040 carbon-free electricity target); she offered no direct gas-price measure beyond linking fuel costs to ending the Iran war.
Fraud: her debate support for an independent inspector general referred to Minnesota's state office; only the federal inspector-general and penalty items are recorded.

Jobs and Abortion items come from BallotReady's summary of her campaign priorities page (peggyflanagan.com/priorities could not be fetched directly); the $17 minimum wage is also reported in Minnesota Reformer/KAXE debate coverage.
Gun-ban detail is her own quote inside a Giffords PAC endorsement release (Sept 2026).

'2025 reconciliation law' is the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which she calls the 'Big Ugly Bill'; she also pledged to repeal its tax cuts for the wealthy and lift the Social Security payroll cap above $250,000 (taxes not in the top 10).
